observations.statement: Relative inversion uses full S-pseudorandomness, fixed domination scaling, and a normalized interval-to-group norm comparison with its density factor. The diagonal cutoff is chosen only after the finite inverse-theorem families and correlation thresholds; it is constant at each physical-scale stage, avoiding an implicit cutoff equation.

Linear replacement telescopes products under a common ordinary majorant and applies normal-form generalized von Neumann. The auxiliary-variable change is an integer bijection, preserving the convex-region sum up to box volume. Admissible residue mass is bounded by the convergent local factors, so the number of residues does not amplify errors.

The local cube calculation uses pairwise nonproportional affine forms after wraparound partition and the proved linear replacement. Ordinary-prime correlation supplies the remaining local factors; primes dividing the step give the explicit logarithmic cutoff loss. No independent Artin correlation theorem is assumed.

Polynomial transference uses the arbitrary-function dense model and rescales its bounded difference before bounded concatenation. Boundary strips are controlled by weighted second moments from the polynomial-forms majorant, including negative coefficients and an enlarged period, not a pointwise logarithmic bound. Fixed-strip limits precede the final diagonal in T.

The fixed-field polynomial count checks the precise Tao–Ziegler model, concatenation and counting parameters, fixes complexities before the cutoff, and retains the actual conditional density instead of model one. Distinct leading coefficients, bounded residue mass and the convergent singular product complete the transfer. Published and preprint numbering are distinguished.

The ray-class lower bound uses published existence/reciprocity and the modulus exact sequence for the maximal Gaussian order. Principality gives the explicit residue-unit quotient. Congruences at 16 and 7 separate the two conjugate classes, while norm-one local groups and the maximal abelian subfield control the surviving conditional density.
